subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A competitive inhibitor reduces the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction by:
options: permanently denaturing the enzyme
binding away from the active site and changing the active site shape
increasing the Vmax of the reaction
binding to the active site, having a similar shape to the substrate
questions.explain: A competitive inhibitor has a complementary shape to the active site and competes with substrate for it; its effect is overcome by raising substrate concentration.

questions.q: Why can small non-polar molecules such as oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by simple diffusion?
options: They require carrier proteins
They are small and non-polar, so they dissolve in and pass through the hydrophobic phospholipid bilayer
They are repelled by the hydrophobic core
They are actively transported
questions.explain: Being small and non-polar, these molecules dissolve in the lipid bilayer and diffuse directly across down their gradient.

questions.q: In an enzyme-catalysed reaction, doubling the enzyme concentration while keeping substrate in large excess will:
options: halve the rate
cause denaturation
have no effect on the initial rate
approximately double the initial rate of reaction
questions.explain: With excess substrate, the number of available active sites limits the rate, so doubling enzyme concentration roughly doubles the rate.

questions.q: In the co-transport of glucose in the ileum, glucose is absorbed into the epithelial cell because:
options: a sodium-glucose co-transporter carries glucose in alongside Na+ moving down its gradient
glucose is actively pumped out of the cell
glucose diffuses freely through the phospholipid bilayer
glucose is pumped directly by ATP into the cell
questions.explain: Na+ entering down its gradient (maintained by the Na+/K+ pump) drives glucose into the cell against its gradient via the co-transporter.

questions.q: Meiosis generates genetic variation partly through independent assortment, which occurs because:
options: maternal and paternal chromosomes orient randomly at the metaphase plate, so combinations in gametes vary
sister chromatids fail to separate
DNA is replicated twice
homologous chromosomes exchange alleles by crossing over
questions.explain: The random orientation of homologous pairs in metaphase I means each gamete receives a different mix of maternal and paternal chromosomes.

questions.q: The Golgi apparatus is mainly responsible for:
options: synthesising ribosomal RNA
modifying, packaging and sorting proteins into vesicles for secretion
producing ATP
replicating DNA
questions.explain: The Golgi modifies proteins (e.g. adding carbohydrate), packages them into vesicles and labels them for their destination.

questions.q: A change in pH away from the optimum reduces enzyme activity because:
options: it permanently increases enzyme concentration
it increases the kinetic energy of the substrate
it lowers the activation energy
H+ or OH- ions disrupt ionic and hydrogen bonds, altering active site shape
questions.explain: Changes in pH alter charges on R-groups and disrupt bonds maintaining the tertiary structure, distorting the active site.

questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium across a membrane during diffusion:
options: ATP is consumed continuously
molecules move only from low to high concentration
molecules continue to move in both directions but there is no net movement
all movement of molecules stops
questions.explain: At equilibrium molecules still move randomly both ways, but with equal rates so there is no net change in concentration.

questions.q: Which factor would increase the permeability of a cell membrane?
options: Removal of all membrane proteins
A decrease in temperature, increasing phospholipid order
An increase in temperature, increasing phospholipid movement and creating gaps
Increasing cholesterol content
questions.explain: Higher temperatures increase phospholipid kinetic energy and fluidity, and can denature membrane proteins, increasing permeability.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes RNA from DNA?
options: RNA is double-stranded and helical
RNA nucleotides are joined by ester bonds, not phosphodiester bonds
RNA contains ribose and uracil
RNA contains thymine instead of uracil
questions.explain: RNA uses the pentose ribose and the base uracil in place of thymine, and is typically single-stranded.

questions.q: ATP is described as the universal energy currency because:
options: it cannot be regenerated once hydrolysed
hydrolysis of its terminal phosphate releases a manageable quantity of energy for cellular reactions
it stores energy long-term like glycogen
its hydrolysis releases a large, fixed amount of energy in a single immediate step
questions.explain: ATP releases a small, usable amount of energy when its terminal phosphate bond is hydrolysed to ADP and Pi, and is rapidly resynthesised.

questions.q: A transmission electron microscope (TEM) differs from a scanning electron microscope (SEM) in that the TEM:
options: can be used on living specimens
produces a 3D surface image
has lower resolution than the SEM
passes electrons through a thin specimen to give a high-resolution 2D image of internal structure
questions.explain: A TEM transmits electrons through an ultra-thin section, producing a detailed 2D image of internal ultrastructure, whereas an SEM gives a 3D surface view.
